Subject: SOC2 evidence & cross-border hosting - FinTrust due diligence

Hi Evelyn,

FinTrust is kicking off our vendor due diligence for the inference layer. Attached is our standard vendor questionnaire (FinTrust_Vendor_Q.pdf). We have a few immediate asks so procurement can clear us for a pilot: 

1) SOC 2 Type II report (most recent available; redacted is fine) and the covered audit period.
2) A short bridge letter confirming how Redwood handles hosting for UK/EU customers and whether customer data ever resides or is accessible from the US.
3) Confirmation of SCCs or transfer mechanisms and whether customer keys/KMS are available.
4) Subprocessor list and where those subprocessors host customer data.

Can you confirm whether you can get items 1–3 to us within 10 business days? Procurement will also want a one-page summary we can attach to the PO.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Price
Vendor Risk Analyst | FinTrust Bank

High-level plan and timeline:
- By Sep 9: provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II (most recent report), a one-page summary tailored for procurement, and a draft bridge letter for your legal team to review.
- By Sep 12: provide subprocessor list and confirmation of SCCs / DPA clauses; if you need a signed bridge letter we can route via DocuSign.

Quick answers to the bullets so you have context before we send artifacts:
- SOC 2: we will provide a redacted report covering the latest 12-month period (audit period included in the header).
- Hosting: Redwood’s hosted API is multi-region. For customers based in the EU/UK we offer an EU data plane option; we can confirm whether the account is configured for EU-only hosting and provide a short attestation in the bridge letter.
- Transfers: we use SCCs for transfers when applicable; there are options to enable customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private.

If possible, can we book a short call to walk procurement/legal through the one-pager? I can make time Sep 12 in the afternoon (BST).

Regards,

Hi all — adding technical detail so FinTrust has what you need for vendor risk. Short summary below; I can supply an architecture diagram and network flow if helpful.

1) Scope & audit period: The SOC 2 Type II we will share covers Redwood’s hosted inference control environment for the audit period Apr 1, 2025 – Mar 31, 2026. The report is redacted for customer IDs and some operational details.

2) Hosting regions & data residency:
- Hosted API: accounts can be configured to use an EU data plane; when configured, production inference requests and cached artifacts are stored in EU cloud regions (Azure/EU or GCP/EU regions depending on capacity).
- Default public hosted accounts historically use US-backed control plane services for cross-region features (telemetry/ops). We will explicitly attest whether a specific account (FinTrust pilot) is on the EU plane.

3) Cross-border transfers & legal mechanisms:
- We use EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for transfers where required. For customers requiring extra guarantees we offer Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private deployments to ensure data remains in the customer’s region.
- Metrics and aggregated telemetry are pseudonymized; no customer plaintext data is included in analytics exports.

4) Key/Encryption options:
- Encryption at rest by default; customer-managed keys via KMS available for Dedicated and Private.

5) Subprocessors: I will attach the latest subprocessors spreadsheet and mark which ones host EU customer data.

Planned attachments: subprocessors_2026.xlsx (redacted), short network flow diagram (PDF).

If FinTrust needs a line-by-line confirmation in the bridge letter ("data stays in EU region X and is not exported to US"), we can provide an account-specific attestation once we confirm the account configuration.

—Rishi
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: subprocessors_2026.xlsx (3 rows redacted)]
